To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the light-front spin dependent spectral functions of a spin-1/2 system are related to three independent leading twist T-even quark transverse momentum distributions and that the neutron transverse momentum distributions can be accessed in semi-inclusive deep-inelastic electron scattering off 3He in the Bjorkn limit.

(1) the light-front dynamics provides a covariant framework for the study of the quark TMDs in the nucleon and (2) the light-front spin spectral function of a 3He nucleus can be measured through a semi-inclusive deep-inelastic electron scattering off a polarized 3 He target.

(i) the neutron transverse-momentum distribution functions are related to the light-front spin dependent spectral function of 3He; (ii) the neutron T-even transverse momentum distribution functions can be extracted from semi-inclusive electron scattering off polarised 3He; and (iii) the T-even transverse momenta distributions are related to the transverse spin distribution of the quarks within 3He, and to the transverse momentum distribution of the quark within the neutron.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the spin structure of hadrons in terms of the quark and gluon degrees of freedom.
a systematic analysis of the light-front structure of the nucleon.

the study of the structure of the nucleon and its excited states in a relativistic framework, with the aim of understanding the origin of nucleon mass and spin, and of providing a theoretical basis for the analysis of the experimental data from the Jefferson Laboratory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the light-front Hamiltonian dynamics provides a very powerful and flexible theoretical framework to analyze the transverse-momentum distribution functions in a nucleon and to extract them from experimental data.

the light-front dynamics, which has been successfully applied to a large class of nuclear and hadron structure problems, is also well suited for the description of the quark transversal motion in the neutron.
the light-front dynamics is a useful and powerful tool to study the transverse-momentum structure of hadrons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the light-front dynamics, in contrast with the covariant dynamics, allows us to identify the transverse-momentum distribution of a J =1/2 system with the spin-dependent spectral function.

the neutron transverse-momentum distribution can be obtained from a measurement of the semi-inclusive cross section for the scattering of a longitudinally polarized electron off an unpolarized 3He nucleus.

the transverse-momentum distribution of the nucleon is a consequence of the spin-dependent spectral function, which is a function of the nucleon light-front momentum fraction and transverse momentum, the light-front spin projection of the nucleon, and the light-front helicity of the nucleon.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the light-front dynamics provides a natural framework to describe the spin structure of the nucleon and the spin-dependent structure functions of nuclei.
